correctness.rationale: For integers a,b>=2, faces split according to the zero, one or both shared vertices u,v. The no-shared-vertex part is X=skel1(Delta^A)*skel1(Delta^B), the one-shared-vertex parts are two cones on the connected K_{a,b}, and the both-shared part is only the edge uv. The graphs skel1(Delta^A) and skel1(Delta^B) are connected, so X is simply connected and indeed two-connected; inclusion K_{a,b}->X is nullhomotopic, permitting two actual cofibration/mapping-cone splittings. The final edge joins two points already connected and contributes one S1. Graph cycle ranks C(a-1,2), C(b-1,2) yield X a wedge of their product many S3, and K_{a,b} has rank (a-1)(b-1), yielding twice that many S2. The integral wedge argument includes a=b=2 and zero S3 cases. Independent combinatorial graph adjacency and triangle prohibition enumeration reconstructed 16 full face-count polynomials for 2<=a,b<=5; those finite counts do not assert integral or infinite proofs.
